C11 and C18 likewise provide related rhetoric but no materially parallel sequence or distinctive shared language sufficient to establish a drafting-template relationship.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"This tremendous gain in our strength has been made necessary by the lawless aggression of communist forces in Korea, and by the menace of still further communist attacks against other free nations.","parent_excerpt":"It is essential to our national security that we build up our defenses as quickly and vigorously as possible. We do not know what further aggressive plans may be in the making by the adversaries of the free world.","explanation":"C07 closely parallels the justification for rapid defense buildup, but the language expresses a general contemporary policy rationale rather than a distinctive drafting formula."},{"child_excerpt":"The speed with which we have been able to strengthen our defenses should be a source of inspiration and encouragement to men everywhere who love freedom.","parent_excerpt":"the increasing menace of the forces of communist aggression requires that the national defense of the United States be strengthened as speedily as possible","explanation":"C11 shares the combination of communist aggression and speedy strengthening of defense, but not the child’s commendatory letter structure or concrete report-based framing."},{"child_excerpt":"It is evidence of our determination, in company with other free nations, to establish and maintain world peace.","parent_excerpt":"It is now clear that the free nations must accelerate the efforts they are making to strengthen their common security.","explanation":"C18 contains similar free-nation collective-defense rhetoric, but its detailed appropriations request and administrative substance are not reused in the child."}]}
